basis: Brain malformations and developmental delay define neurologic disease; hypospadias in 4/4 males is a urethral malformation. Other genital findings are reproductive.

decisions.renal: primary: hypospadias affects the urethra, explicitly covered by renal, and occurs in 4/4 reported males.

basis: Intellectual disability defines the disorder; hearing impairment and bilateral ptosis each occur in 1/3. Ptosis represents eyelid dysfunction; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.

decisions.ocular: involved: bilateral ptosis is persistent eyelid dysfunction, reported in 1/3 patients; cerebral visual impairment belongs to neurologic.

basis: Viral acute liver failure with defining hepatic encephalopathy; impaired clotting-factor synthesis causes coagulopathy in essentially all cases and is a major diagnostic criterion.

decisions.haematologic: involved: coagulopathy is an acute liver failure diagnostic criterion, present in essentially all cases, with loss of coagulation function.

basis: Lower motor neuron disease causes chronic denervation. Hand muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99% but reflects loss of neural input, without a direct muscle disease process.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy in 80-99% is secondary to motor neuron denervation; the disease directly targets neurons, without intrinsic muscle injury.

basis: Sporadic endogenous prion misfolding causes destructive CNS degeneration. Transmissibility alone does not establish infection; aspiration pneumonia and sepsis are separate secondary diseases.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: sporadic disease arises through endogenous prion misfolding; transmission potential alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism in this subtype.

basis: Severe Hallermann-Streiff phenotype supports ocular, craniofacial skeletal and skin defects; dental abnormalities are a major diagnostic feature. Evidence is limited to one family.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental abnormalities are a major diagnostic feature of the Hallermann-Streiff phenotype specified by the definition; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: skin atrophy and hypotrichosis are defining features of the Hallermann-Streiff phenotype, of which this is a severe form.

basis: Aniridia, intellectual disability and obesity define WAGRO; proteinuria in 1/2 supports intrinsic renal involvement. Exostoses and hypertension, each 1/2, omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: proteinuria in 1/2 supports renal dysfunction beyond Wilms tumour predisposition; the three primary slots retain the universal defining features.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly syndrome-defining and occurs in 3/3 reported patients.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: obesity defines this WAGR subphenotype and occurs in 2/2; it establishes the metabolic axis.

basis: Manganese transport disorder causes progressive neurologic injury. Contractures (3/9) and scoliosis (30-79%) are secondary to dystonia/spasticity, without established direct musculoskeletal injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contractures (3/9) and scoliosis (30-79%) are secondary mechanical consequences of neurologic dysfunction; direct bone, joint or muscle disease is not established.

basis: Glycosylation defect with severe CNS disease; ocular abnormalities and liver dysfunction occur in 30-79%. GI findings lack specified direct injury; bone and hearing findings omitted at cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: decreased liver function is explicitly frequent (30-79%), establishing functional hepatic involvement.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the 80-99% annotation is nonspecific; feeding difficulties do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage. Definite hepatic dysfunction takes priority.

basis: Autoimmune encephalopathy; supplied HPO identifies cerebral vasculitis in 80-99%, supporting direct vascular involvement. Associated Hashimoto thyroiditis is a separate disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: supplied HPO explicitly reports cerebral vasculitis in 80-99%; vascular inflammation satisfies direct damage and frequency requirements.
